findings.reason: printed_height is derived from the hypothetical GPU D bounding box (d_base + d['thickness'] + 8.0 = 200mm in compact, 249mm in universal) rather than the actual printed parts. Since the 4 gap posts and D-beams terminate at beam_top (150mm compact, 199mm universal), the actual built BRep solid has core.BoundBox.ZLength == 150.0mm. In build(), line 184 checks 'any(abs(a-b) > 1e-6 for a, b in zip(actual, layout[\"printed_bbox_mm\"]))', which will raise RuntimeError('Actual geometry differs from declared print bounds') due to a 50mm mismatch. The print bbox must reflect actual printed parts, not GPU envelope height.

findings.minimal_fix:
def test_core_bbox_derived_not_gpu_top():
    layout = plan_layout(default_config('compact'))
    bbox = layout['core_bbox_mm']
    dims = layout['dimensions']
    
    assert math.isclose(bbox[0], dims['core_width_mm'], abs_tol=1e-6)
    assert math.isclose(bbox[1], dims['core_depth_mm'], abs_tol=1e-6)
    assert math.isclose(bbox[2], layout['beam_top_mm'], abs_tol=1e-6)
findings.reason: test_core_bbox_derived_not_gpu_top asserts weak upper bound 'bbox[2] <= 254.0' rather than asserting equality with the actual derived printed core height (beam_top_mm = 150.0), allowing the GPU top (200.0) bug in plan_layout to silently pass.
